spans.s:
Tṛṇa, ‘grass,’ is often mentioned in the Rigveda and later. It was used as straw to roof in a house or hut.
Foot notes i. 161, 1; 162, 8, 11; x. 102, 10, etc.
Av. ii. 30, 1; vi. 54, 1, etc.; aitareya brāhmaṇa, iii. 22; viii. 24, etc.
Av. iii. 12, 5; ix. 3, 4, 7.
Tṛṇa-jalāyuka, ‘caterpillar,’ is mentioned in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad (iv. 2, 4).

Tṛṇa-skanda occurs once in the Rigveda as the name of a prince, his subjects (viśaḥ) being referred to. The word may originally have meant ‘grasshopper.’
Foot notes i. 172, 3.
Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 159, takes viśaḥ as ‘cantons,’ but see viś.
St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.
